approval: draft for the author's approval; the generator marks every edition draft until status reads approved
note: What each marked element is for, listed under each figure by its mark number. One entry per mark target (the control's AutomationId); the figure keeps the control's visible text as its label. Each purpose says only what its sources state.

purposes.purpose: Draws the detector face for the current settings: the static crystal gain pattern with its colour scale and the dead gaps between the pixels. Its area is geometry only, not the acquired count rate.
Says whose settings the face and the facts beside it show: the settings for the next acquisition, or, once data exist, the acquired settings, locked until Reset.
Reads out the flood-map pixel under the pointer: its centre in mm and its value, so a position can be read off the image.
Holds the readout choice — the default direct crystal assignment or the experimental physical readout — with its calibration preparation and energy window.
Holds the engineering geometry of the mask and the detector: a preset and the five values it sets.
Holds the source list and the fields of the selected source. Sources are edited here before an acquisition; while acquired data exist they stay locked until Reset.

A row of the measurement table: its number, the image it was drawn on, its kind (distance, angle or ROI) and its value. Selecting a row describes it under the table; Delete or the row's delete button removes it.

A row of the measurement table: its number, the image it was drawn on, its kind (distance, angle or ROI) and its value. Selecting a row describes it under the table; Delete or the row's delete button removes it.

A row of the measurement table: its number, the image it was drawn on, its kind (distance, angle or ROI) and its value. Selecting a row describes it under the table; Delete or the row's delete button removes it.
Describes the selected measurement: its coordinates, size and, for an ROI, its pixel count and pixel statistics.
Closes the dialog without acting: the reset confirmation keeps the acquisition, the Options dialog discards its draft. Escape does the same.
The width of one mask cell, in mm (at least 0.05 mm).
The distance between the mask and the detector, in mm (at least 1 mm). Every source must lie beyond the mask's front face.
States why the optics values are refused. While it shows, Start is refused and the status bar gives the same reason.
The centre-to-centre spacing of the detector pixels, in mm (at least 0.05 mm, and larger than the reflector gap set in Options).
The number of detector pixels along each side of the square array, an integer from 4 to 64.

Picks an engineering geometry — Sharp (the default), Baseline, Wide FOV or High-res — that writes all five values and keeps them read-only; Custom makes them editable, starting from the current values. A preset does not move the sources.
The prime rank of the MURA mask pattern: 5, 7, 11, 13, 17, 19 or 23. With the cell pitch and the mask–detector distance it sets the nominal field of view and the resolution element.
Selects the left Detector tab and puts the keyboard focus on the readout choice, where the experimental physical readout can be chosen.
Says why this view is empty: it shows the experimental physical readout, and the default direct crystal assignment has none.
Shows the SiPM footprints and the illustrative charge-division circuit of the experimental physical readout.
Confirms the reset: the acquired data, images, spectrum and the scene frozen at Start are discarded, the status returns to Ready and the inputs unlock. Measurement shapes are kept.
Names the live time and counts a reset would discard and says that the inputs unlock for the next acquisition.
The activity of the selected source, in µCi; a value of 0 or less becomes 1 µCi.
The distance of the selected source from the detector plane, in mm; values outside 200–3000 mm are clamped.
The isotope the selected source emits, chosen from the engine's isotope list.
The lateral offset of the selected source from the camera axis along x, in mm; the offset is what sets the source's off-axis angle.
The lateral offset of the selected source from the camera axis along y, in mm; the offset is what sets the source's off-axis angle.
Switches the counts axis between logarithmic (the default) and linear. It is a view setting: the acquired data do not change.
Sets each line's energy window to N times the FWHM at that line (default 1.5). The bands and the line table recount from the acquired events, and Imaging uses the same N.

Starts an acquisition over the preset live time. Once data exist it reads Continue and resumes the same acquisition while the acquired live time is below the preset. A refused Start states its reason in the status bar.
The run status line: Ready, or the state with live time, counts, count rate (counts ÷ live time) and seed. A refused Start is stated here in the warning colour, a failure as Failed with its message.
sources: docs/VV.Studio.SRS.md SR-RUN-03, SR-RUN-13, SR-RUN-25, SR-RUN-28, §5 (status messages)

purposes.purpose: Ends the running acquisition and keeps everything acquired; the inputs stay locked and the button then offers Continue.
Shows the four readout outputs A–D and their sum for a selected event of the experimental physical readout.
Shows the detector face for the current settings and, with the experimental physical readout, its SiPM, Anger, calibration and diagnostics views.

Shows the detector flood map and the decoded reconstruction, with distance, angle and ROI measurements in mm. All four workspaces show the same acquisition; switching changes only the view (Ctrl+1 to Ctrl+4).
Shows the histogram of measured energies (0–2000 keV) with a band at each emission line and a table of the counts inside each band.
Shows the simulated ADC and shaped pulse traces of a selected acquired event, or, with the experimental physical readout, its four outputs A–D.
